decisions.choice: Jehoiakim: the name the Hebrew text has here, although the events of the chapter belong to the reign of Zedekiah
alternatives: In the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah son of Josiah
decisions.reason: The envoys come to Zedekiah (verse 3), Jeremiah speaks to Zedekiah (verse 12), and Jeconiah has already been taken to Babylon (verse 20), which happened in 597 BC, after Jehoiakim had died. The next chapter dates the same events "in that year, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year" (28:1). A few Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac translation read "Zedekiah" here, and the Greek translation has no verse 1 at all. The heading is word for word the one at 26:1, and a copyist may have repeated it from there. The Hebrew is printed as it stands, but the reign meant is probably Zedekiah's.

decisions.choice: the beginning of the reign: the early part of a king's rule
decisions.reason: The phrase need not mean the first months. In 28:1 the same words cover the fourth year of Zedekiah, about 594 BC.

decisions.choice: this word: a heading over the whole chapter, which Jeremiah then tells in his own voice
decisions.reason: From verse 2 Jeremiah speaks of himself ("the LORD said to me", verses 2, 12, 16). The heading introduces three messages on one theme: to the foreign kings (verses 2-11), to Zedekiah (verses 12-15), and to the priests and people (verses 16-22).

decisions.choice: this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying (Literal); this message came to Jeremiah from the LORD (Balanced); the LORD gave Jeremiah this message (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this heading throughout Jeremiah, with "this" as the Hebrew has it.

decisions.choice: Yehoyakimu
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names Jehoiakim here, though the chapter is set under Zedekiah (verses 3 and 12); Swahili keeps the name of the text, as the English does, and meaning decision m1 explains it.

decisions.choice: straps and yoke bars: the parts of a yoke such as oxen wore
decisions.reason: A yoke was a wooden bar laid across an animal's neck and tied on with cords or leather straps (Leviticus 26:13; Ezekiel 34:27 name the same two parts). The plural may describe one yoke made of several pieces, or several yokes, since verse 3 sends them to five kings. In 28:10 the prophet Hananiah takes the yoke bar off Jeremiah's neck and breaks it.

decisions.choice: a sign acted out: the yoke on the prophet's neck stands for submission to the king of Babylon
decisions.reason: As with the loincloth (13:1-11) and the clay jar (19:1-13), Jeremiah carries God's message in an action. Verses 8, 11 and 12 say what it means: to put one's neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon is to accept his rule.

decisions.choice: Thus said the LORD to me (Literal); The LORD said this to me (Balanced); This is what the LORD said to me (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 13:1. God's words to Jeremiah open a double quotation mark here, which stays open to the end of verse 11.

decisions.choice: wooden yoke bars and leather straps to tie them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the two parts were made of and how they fit together, so that the reader can picture a yoke.

decisions.choice: correas y barras de yugo
decisions.reason: The parts of an ox's yoke (meaning decision m1) keep the wording the terms note sets for 27:2; Readable says what they were made of, as the English does.

decisions.choice: nira
decisions.reason: "Nira" for the yoke, as 1 Kings 12:4, at every level, so the sign and the message about the king of Babylon's yoke use one word.

en.R: Then send them to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre and Sidon. Send them with the messengers these kings have sent to Jerusalem to meet Zedekiah king of Judah.

decisions.choice: send them: the straps and yoke bars themselves
decisions.reason: "Them" points back to the pieces of the yoke in verse 2, so each king receives the sign along with the message. Some take it more loosely as "send word", but the pronoun has the yoke as its nearest object.

decisions.choice: five neighboring kingdoms whose envoys had gathered in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Edom, Moab and Ammon lay east and south-east of Judah; Tyre and Sidon were the Phoenician ports on the coast to the north. Their envoys at Zedekiah's court were most likely planning a joint revolt against Babylon, about 594 BC (28:1). The same kings are named among those who must drink the cup of God's anger (25:21-22). "The sons of Ammon" is the usual name for the Ammonites.

decisions.choice: the Ammonites (Balanced), Ammon (Readable); envoys (Balanced), messengers (Readable); these kings have sent (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Sons of Ammon" is the people's name. The messengers here are royal ambassadors, so Balanced calls them envoys. Verse 4 calls the kings "their masters", so Readable says the kings had sent them.

decisions.choice: their masters: the kings who sent the envoys
decisions.reason: The word is used of a lord or master, and of a king by those who serve him. The envoys are their kings' servants.

decisions.choice: three layers of speech: God to Jeremiah, Jeremiah to the envoys, the envoys to their kings
decisions.reason: God tells Jeremiah what to say to the envoys (verses 2-11). Jeremiah gives them the LORD's words, which they are to repeat to their kings (verses 5-11).

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, speaks to foreign kings
decisions.reason: The God of a small kingdom gives orders to the rulers of its neighbors. Verse 5 gives the reason he can: he made the earth and gives it to whom he chooses.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for the message given to the envoys, to the end of verse 11; no further marks for the words to the kings
decisions.reason: God's words to Jeremiah are already in double marks, so the message Jeremiah passes on takes single marks. The words the envoys are to repeat follow "Say this to your masters" after a colon, as God's words follow "Thus says the LORD" elsewhere in Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: command them [to speak] to (Literal); give them this charge for (Balanced); tell them to take this message to their kings (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Command them to their masters" means to give the envoys a message to carry home. Readable says "kings" for "masters" (see m1).

decisions.choice: the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, Balanced and Readable say "Armies" for "hosts" (see Isaiah 1:9).

decisions.choice: “ ” for the message given to the envoys, to the end of verse 11
decisions.reason: Three layers of speech (meaning decision m2): the LORD's words to Jeremiah take « », the message for the envoys “ ”, and the words the envoys are to repeat to their kings take no further marks, as the English does.

source.text: אָנֹכִ֞י עָשִׂ֣יתִי אֶת־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֶת־הָאָדָ֤ם וְאֶת־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ בְּכֹחִי֙ הַגָּד֔וֹל וּבִזְרוֹעִ֖י הַנְּטוּיָ֑ה וּנְתַתִּ֕יהָ לַאֲשֶׁ֖ר יָשַׁ֥ר בְּעֵינָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: I, I made the earth, the human and the animal which [are] on [the] face of the earth, by my power the great and by my arm the outstretched, and I give it to whom it is right in my eyes.

en.L: I made the earth, {{gender:humankind|man}} and the animals that [are] on the face of the earth, by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great power and by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} outstretched arm, and I give it to whomever it is right in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes.
en.B: It is I who made the earth, and the people and animals that live on it, by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great power and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} outstretched arm, and I give it to anyone I see fit.
en.R: I made the earth, and the people and animals that live on it. I did it by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great power and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} strong arm. And I give the earth to anyone I choose.

es.L: Yo hice la tierra, al ser humano y a los animales que [están] sobre la faz de la tierra, con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} gran poder y con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} brazo extendido, y la doy a quien es recto ante {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ojos.
es.B: Soy yo quien hizo la tierra, y a la gente y los animales que viven en ella, con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} gran poder y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} brazo extendido, y se la doy a quien me parece bien.
es.R: Yo hice la tierra, y a la gente y los animales que viven en ella. Lo hice con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} gran poder y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} brazo fuerte. Y le doy la tierra a quien yo quiero.

sw.L: Mimi nimeiumba dunia, wanadamu na wanyama walio juu ya uso wa dunia, kwa nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} kuu na kwa mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ulionyoshwa, nami ninaitoa kwa yeyote aliye sawa machoni {{deity_pronoun:pangu|Pangu}}.
sw.B: Ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niliyeiumba dunia, na watu na wanyama wanaoishi juu yake, kwa nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} kuu na mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ulionyoshwa, nami ninaitoa kwa yeyote ninayeona inafaa.
sw.R: Mimi niliiumba dunia, na watu na wanyama wanaoishi juu yake. Niliifanya kwa nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} kuu na mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wenye nguvu. Nami ninaitoa dunia kwa yeyote ninayemchagua.

decisions.choice: I: written out and placed first, for emphasis
decisions.reason: The pronoun is not needed with the verb, so it stresses the speaker: it is the Creator who speaks, and his right to give the earth away rests on his having made it.

decisions.choice: great power and outstretched arm: God's strength at work
decisions.reason: The words recall the exodus, where God brought Israel out "with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm" (Deuteronomy 4:34; 9:29). Jeremiah uses the same pair of creation in 32:17.

decisions.choice: to whomever it is right in my eyes: to whomever I judge fit
decisions.reason: "In my eyes" means "in my judgment". Rule over the earth is God's gift, given as he decides. Daniel 4:14 says the same of the Most High, who gives kingship to whom he wishes.

decisions.choice: anyone I see fit (Balanced); anyone I choose (Readable)
decisions.reason: The idiom of the eyes becomes plain English for judging or choosing. Balanced keeps the emphasis of verse 5 with "It is I who".

decisions.choice: strong arm
decisions.reason: Readable says "strong" because a stretched-out arm is a picture of strength put to work.

decisions.choice: al ser humano
decisions.reason: Literal says "el ser humano" for *ha'adam*, which already includes women, so no gender span is needed where the English has one.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה אָֽנֹכִי֙ נָתַ֨תִּי֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָאֲרָצ֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה בְּיַ֛ד נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל עַבְדִּ֑י וְגַם֙ אֶת־חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה נָתַ֥תִּי ל֖וֹ לְעָבְדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now I, I give all the lands the these into [the] hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon my servant, and also [the] animals of the field I give to him to serve him.

en.L: And now I have given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant; and even the animals of the field I have given to him to serve him.
en.B: Now I have handed all these lands over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant. I have even given him the wild animals to serve him.
en.R: Now I have put all these countries under the power of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant. I have even given him the wild animals, so that they will serve him too.

es.L: Y ahora yo he entregado todas estas tierras en mano de Nabucodonosor, rey de Babilonia, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo; y aun las bestias del campo le he dado para que le sirvan.
es.B: Ahora he entregado todas estas tierras a Nabucodonosor, rey de Babilonia, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo. Incluso le he dado los animales salvajes para que le sirvan.
es.R: Ahora he puesto todos estos países bajo el poder de Nabucodonosor, rey de Babilonia. Él es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo. Incluso le he dado los animales salvajes, para que también le sirvan.

sw.L: Na sasa nimeitia nchi hizi zote mkononi mwa Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli, mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}; na hata wanyama wa porini nimempa ili wamtumikie.
sw.B: Sasa nimeikabidhi nchi hizi zote kwa Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli, mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Nimempa hata wanyama wa porini wamtumikie.
sw.R: Sasa nimeziweka nchi hizi zote chini ya mamlaka ya Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli. Yeye ni mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Nimempa hata wanyama wa porini, ili nao wamtumikie.

decisions.choice: my servant: Nebuchadnezzar as the one through whom God carries out his purpose
decisions.reason: The title does not mean that the king worshiped Israel's God. It means he does God's work, here the work of judgment, as in 25:9 and 43:10. Isaiah speaks in the same way of Assyria as the rod of God's anger (Isaiah 10:5-7) and of Cyrus as his anointed (Isaiah 45:1).

decisions.choice: I have given: a decision already made and now in force
decisions.reason: The verb describes God's gift as settled. It can also be read as a present, "I am giving"; either way, the lands are already in the king's hand by God's will. "And now" turns from creation (verse 5) to the present moment.

decisions.choice: even the animals of the field: his rule reaches everything, even wild creatures
decisions.reason: The animals of the field are the wild animals, as against the herds. Giving them to the king shows how complete his rule is meant to be (28:14; Daniel 2:38).

decisions.choice: Nebuchadnezzar: the form of the name used in this chapter
decisions.reason: Jeremiah usually spells the name Nebuchadrezzar (21:2; 25:9), closer to its Babylonian form, Nabu-kudurri-usur. Chapters 27-29 use Nebuchadnezzar, as Kings does. Both name the same king, who ruled Babylon from 605 to 562 BC.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: As in 7:25, "servant" is kept at every level for one who serves God's purpose; it describes his role, not ownership by a master.

decisions.choice: handed ... over to (Balanced), put ... under the power of (Readable); wild animals
decisions.reason: "Into the hand of" means into someone's control. "The animals of the field" are the wild animals.

decisions.choice: Nabucodonosor
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of this chapter has the form with -n- (meaning decision m4), so every level writes the usual "Nabucodonosor"; chapters with the -r- form have "Nabucodorosor".

decisions.choice: Nebukadneza
decisions.reason: In chapters 27-29 the Hebrew spells the king's name with n, so Swahili uses "Nebukadneza" as Kings does, where 21-25 had "Nebukadreza"; he is the same king.

source.text: וְעָבְד֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְאֶת־בְּנ֖וֹ וְאֶֽת־בֶּן־בְּנ֑וֹ עַ֣ד בֹּא־עֵ֤ת אַרְצוֹ֙ גַּם־ה֔וּא וְעָ֤בְדוּ בוֹ֙ גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֔ים וּמְלָכִ֖ים גְּדֹלִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And will serve him all the nations, and his son and [the] son of his son, until comes [the] time of his land, also he; and will make serve by him nations many and kings great.

en.L: And all the nations shall serve him and his son and his son's son, until the time of his own land comes, [his] also; and then many nations and great kings shall make him serve [them].
en.B: All the nations will serve him and his son and his grandson, until the time comes for his own land as well. Then many nations and great kings will make him serve them.
en.R: All the nations will serve him, and his son and his grandson after him. But a time will come for his own country too. Then many nations and powerful kings will make Babylon serve them.

es.L: Y todas las naciones le servirán a él, a su hijo y al hijo de su hijo, hasta que llegue también el tiempo de su propia tierra; y entonces muchas naciones y grandes reyes lo harán su siervo.
es.B: Todas las naciones le servirán a él, a su hijo y a su nieto, hasta que llegue también el tiempo de su propia tierra. Entonces muchas naciones y grandes reyes lo harán servirles.
es.R: Todas las naciones le servirán a él, y a su hijo y a su nieto después de él. Pero llegará el tiempo también para su propio país. Entonces muchas naciones y reyes poderosos harán que Babilonia les sirva.

sw.L: Na mataifa yote watamtumikia yeye, na mwanawe, na mwana wa mwanawe, mpaka wakati wa nchi yake mwenyewe utakapofika, [yake] pia; ndipo mataifa mengi na wafalme wakuu watamtumikisha.
sw.B: Mataifa yote yatamtumikia yeye na mwanawe na mjukuu wake, mpaka wakati wa nchi yake mwenyewe pia utakapofika. Ndipo mataifa mengi na wafalme wakuu watamfanya awatumikie.
sw.R: Mataifa yote yatamtumikia yeye, na mwanawe na mjukuu wake baada yake. Lakini wakati utafika kwa nchi yake pia. Ndipo mataifa mengi na wafalme wenye nguvu wataifanya Babeli iwatumikie.

decisions.choice: his son and his son's son: the generations after him, a long but limited span
decisions.reason: The phrase sets a limit on Babylon's power: it will last into the time of his descendants and then end. Babylon fell to Cyrus of Persia in 539 BC, about two generations after Nebuchadnezzar came to power. Jeremiah elsewhere speaks of seventy years (25:11-12; 29:10).

decisions.choice: the time of his land, his too: the time when his own land's turn comes
decisions.reason: "Also he" stresses that Babylon will not escape: as it judged others, its own time of judgment will come (25:12-14; chapters 50-51).

decisions.choice: make him serve: reduce him to service
decisions.reason: The verb "serve" with this preposition means to make someone work for you as a servant or a subject people (25:14; 30:8; Exodus 1:14). The king who made the nations serve will in turn be made to serve. "Him" is the king standing for his kingdom.

decisions.choice: verse 7 is part of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Greek translation has no verse 7. Jeremiah in Greek is shorter in many places (see 1:1). The Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: a time will come for his own country too; Babylon
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "a time will come" and lets the next sentence say what that time is. It says "Babylon" for "him", since the king stands for his kingdom (see m3).

source.text: וְהָיָ֨ה הַגּ֜וֹי וְהַמַּמְלָכָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־יַעַבְד֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ אֶת־נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֔ל וְאֵ֨ת אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־יִתֵּן֙ אֶת־צַוָּאר֔וֹ בְּעֹ֖ל מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֑ל בַּחֶרֶב֩ וּבָרָעָ֨ב וּבַדֶּ֜בֶר אֶפְקֹ֨ד עַל־הַגּ֤וֹי הַהוּא֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה עַד־תֻּמִּ֥י אֹתָ֖ם בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, the nation and the kingdom which not they will serve him, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and which not it will put its neck in [the] yoke of [the] king of Babylon, by the sword and by the famine and by the pestilence I will visit upon the nation the that, declaration of Yahweh, until I have consumed them by his hand.

en.L: And it shall be [that] the nation or the kingdom that will not serve him, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and that will not put its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, with the sword and with famine and with pestilence I will punish that nation, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, until I have finished them off by his hand.
en.B: Any nation or kingdom that will not serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and will not put its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, I will punish with sword, famine and plague, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, until I have finished it off by his hand.
en.R: But suppose a nation or kingdom refuses to serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and will not put its neck under his yoke by accepting his rule. Then I will punish that nation with war, famine and disease, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will use him to destroy it completely.

es.L: Y sucederá que a la nación o al reino que no sirva a él, a Nabucodonosor, rey de Babilonia, y que no ponga su cuello bajo el yugo del rey de Babilonia, con espada, con hambre y con peste castigaré a esa nación, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, hasta que la haya acabado por medio de su mano.
es.B: A cualquier nación o reino que no sirva a Nabucodonosor, rey de Babilonia, y que no ponga su cuello bajo el yugo del rey de Babilonia, la castigaré con la espada, el hambre y la peste, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, hasta acabar con ella por medio de él.
es.R: Pero supongamos que una nación o un reino se niega a servir a Nabucodonosor, rey de Babilonia, y no quiere poner su cuello bajo su yugo aceptando su gobierno. Entonces castigaré a esa nación con la guerra, el hambre y las enfermedades, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Lo usaré a él para destruirla por completo.

sw.L: Na itakuwa, taifa au ufalme usiotaka kumtumikia yeye, Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli, na usiotia shingo yake chini ya nira ya mfalme wa Babeli, kwa upanga na kwa njaa na kwa tauni nitaliadhibu taifa hilo, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mpaka nitakapowamaliza kwa mkono wake.
sw.B: Taifa lolote au ufalme wowote usiotaka kumtumikia Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli, wala kutia shingo yake chini ya nira ya mfalme wa Babeli, nitaliadhibu kwa upanga, njaa na tauni, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mpaka nitakapolimaliza kwa mkono wake.
sw.R: Lakini tuseme taifa au ufalme fulani unakataa kumtumikia Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli, wala hautaki kutia shingo yake chini ya nira yake kwa kukubali utawala wake. Ndipo nitaliadhibu taifa hilo kwa vita, njaa na magonjwa, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nitamtumia yeye kuliangamiza kabisa.

decisions.choice: put its neck under the yoke: submit to his rule
decisions.reason: The picture is the one Jeremiah is wearing (verse 2): a nation that bows its neck to the yoke accepts the king of Babylon as its master.

decisions.choice: punish: deal with a nation for its wrong
decisions.reason: The verb means to attend to someone, and with this preposition it means to call to account and punish (5:9; 9:24). In verse 22 the same verb is used in a good sense.

decisions.choice: until I have finished them off by his hand: the people of that nation destroyed, with Nebuchadnezzar as God's means
decisions.reason: "Them" is the people of the nation; "his hand" is the king of Babylon's. God is the one who acts, and the king is the tool he uses (see verse 6).

decisions.choice: sword, famine and pestilence: war and the hunger and disease that come with siege
decisions.reason: The three come together throughout Jeremiah (14:12; 21:7, 9; 24:10). The third word means a deadly epidemic.

decisions.choice: sword, famine and pestilence (Literal); sword, famine and plague (Balanced); war, famine and disease (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this triad throughout Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: the nation named first and taken up as the object (Balanced); a condition and its result (Readable)
decisions.reason: "It shall be" opens a case. Balanced keeps the nation at the head of the sentence; Readable makes it "suppose ... then" and explains the yoke as accepting his rule.

source.text: וְ֠אַתֶּם אַל־תִּשְׁמְע֨וּ אֶל־נְבִיאֵיכֶ֜ם וְאֶל־קֹֽסְמֵיכֶ֗ם וְאֶל֙ חֲלֹמֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וְאֶל־עֹֽנְנֵיכֶ֖ם וְאֶל־כַּשָּׁפֵיכֶ֑ם אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֞ם אֹמְרִ֤ים אֲלֵיכֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תַעַבְד֖וּ אֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, do not listen to your prophets and to your diviners and to your dreams and to your soothsayers and to your sorcerers, who they [are] saying to you, saying: not you will serve [the] king of Babylon.

en.L: And as for you, do not listen to your prophets, or to your diviners, or to your dreams, or to your soothsayers, or to your sorcerers, who are speaking to you, saying, "You shall not serve the king of Babylon."
en.B: So do not listen to your prophets, your diviners, your dreamers, your fortune-tellers or your sorcerers, who keep telling you, "You will not serve the king of Babylon."
en.R: So do not listen to your prophets, or to people who use magic to learn secret things, or who tell you their dreams, or who tell fortunes, or who practice witchcraft. They keep telling you, "You will not have to serve the king of Babylon."

es.L: Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, no {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchéis}} a {{plural_you:sus profetas|vuestros profetas}}, ni a {{plural_you:sus adivinos|vuestros adivinos}}, ni a {{plural_you:sus sueños|vuestros sueños}}, ni a {{plural_you:sus agoreros|vuestros agoreros}}, ni a {{plural_you:sus hechiceros|vuestros hechiceros}}, que {{plural_you:les|os}} hablan diciendo: «No {{plural_you:servirán|serviréis}} al rey de Babilonia».
es.B: Así que no {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchéis}} a {{plural_you:sus profetas, sus adivinos, sus soñadores, sus agoreros ni sus hechiceros|vuestros profetas, vuestros adivinos, vuestros soñadores, vuestros agoreros ni vuestros hechiceros}}, que siempre {{plural_you:les|os}} están diciendo: «No {{plural_you:servirán|serviréis}} al rey de Babilonia».
es.R: Así que no {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchéis}} a {{plural_you:sus profetas|vuestros profetas}}, ni a los que usan la magia para descubrir cosas secretas, ni a los que {{plural_you:les|os}} cuentan sus sueños, ni a los que adivinan el futuro, ni a los que practican la brujería. Siempre {{plural_you:les|os}} están diciendo: «No {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} que servir al rey de Babilonia».

sw.L: Nanyi, msiwasikilize manabii wenu, wala waaguzi wenu, wala ndoto zenu, wala wapiga ramli wenu, wala wachawi wenu, wanaowaambia, wakisema, "Hamtamtumikia mfalme wa Babeli."
sw.B: Basi msiwasikilize manabii wenu, waaguzi wenu, waota ndoto wenu, wapiga ramli wenu wala wachawi wenu, wanaoendelea kuwaambia, "Hamtamtumikia mfalme wa Babeli."
sw.R: Basi msiwasikilize manabii wenu, wala watu wanaotumia uganga kujua mambo ya siri, wala wanaowaeleza ndoto zao, wala wanaotabiri bahati, wala wanaofanya uchawi. Wanaendelea kuwaambia, "Hamtalazimika kumtumikia mfalme wa Babeli."

decisions.choice: and you: the kings and their peoples, set against their advisers
decisions.reason: The plural pronoun is written out for emphasis. The message goes to the foreign kings through their envoys.

decisions.choice: diviners, soothsayers, sorcerers: people who claimed to learn hidden things or work magic
decisions.reason: These are words from the list of Deuteronomy 18:10-11, practices the nations relied on and Israel was forbidden (Deuteronomy 18:14). The foreign kings trust them, as Judah trusts its own prophets (verse 14).

decisions.choice: your dreams: dreams claimed as messages from heaven, and those who tell them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "your dreams", standing in a list of people; the sense is the dreams and those who report them, as in 23:25-32 and 29:8. Some ancient translations read "your dreamers", which gives the same sense.

decisions.choice: diviners, soothsayers, sorcerers (Literal); diviners, fortune-tellers, sorcerers (Balanced); explained (Readable)
decisions.reason: The words used for these practices in Deuteronomy 18:10 and 14. Balanced says "dreamers" because the list names people; Readable says what each one did.

decisions.choice: double quotation marks for the false prophets' words
decisions.reason: These words stand inside the single-quoted message of verses 4-11, so they take double marks again.

decisions.choice: adivinos, agoreros, hechiceros
decisions.reason: The three kinds of people who claimed to learn hidden things or work magic (meaning decision m2) take three distinct Spanish words at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what each did.

source.text: כִּ֣י שֶׁ֔קֶר הֵ֖ם נִבְּאִ֣ים לָכֶ֑ם לְמַ֨עַן הַרְחִ֤יק אֶתְכֶם֙ מֵעַ֣ל אַדְמַתְכֶ֔ם וְהִדַּחְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם וַאֲבַדְתֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For falsehood they [are] prophesying to you, so as to remove far you from upon your land, and I will drive out you and you will perish.

en.L: For they are prophesying a lie to you, so as to remove you far from your land, and I will drive you out, and you will perish.
en.B: They are prophesying a lie to you, and it will only lead to your being taken far from your land. I will drive you out, and you will perish.
en.R: What they tell you is a lie. It will only get you taken far away from your land. I will drive you out, and you will die.

es.L: Porque mentira {{plural_you:les|os}} profetizan, para {{plural_you:alejarlos|alejaros}} de {{plural_you:su tierra|vuestra tierra}}, y yo {{plural_you:los|os}} echaré y {{plural_you:perecerán|pereceréis}}.
es.B: Lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} profetizan es mentira, y solo servirá para que {{plural_you:los|os}} lleven lejos de {{plural_you:su tierra|vuestra tierra}}. Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} echaré, y {{plural_you:perecerán|pereceréis}}.
es.R: Lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} dicen es mentira. Solo servirá para que {{plural_you:se los lleven|os lleven}} lejos de {{plural_you:su tierra|vuestra tierra}}. Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} echaré, y {{plural_you:morirán|moriréis}}.

sw.L: Kwa maana wanawatabiria uongo, ili kuwahamisha mbali na nchi yenu, nami nitawafukuza, nanyi mtaangamia.
sw.B: Wanawatabiria uongo, nao utawaletea tu kuhamishwa mbali na nchi yenu. Nitawafukuza, nanyi mtaangamia.
sw.R: Wanayowaambia ni uongo. Utawasababisha tu kuchukuliwa mbali na nchi yenu. Nitawafukuza, nanyi mtakufa.

decisions.choice: so as to remove you: the result, not the prophets' aim
decisions.reason: The word can express purpose, but here it gives the outcome: listening to their lies leads to exile. The prophets do not want the people removed; it is what their message will bring about.

decisions.choice: a lie: a message that is false and not from God
decisions.reason: "Lie" is a key word of chapters 27-29 (verses 14, 15, 16; 28:15; 29:9, 21). The prophets are not mistaken guessers; they speak what God has not said.

decisions.choice: it will only lead to (Balanced); it will only get you (Readable)
decisions.reason: These wordings give the sense of result (see m1).

source.text: וְהַגּ֗וֹי אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָבִ֧יא אֶת־צַוָּאר֛וֹ בְּעֹ֥ל מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל וַֽעֲבָד֑וֹ וְהִנַּחְתִּ֤יו עַל־אַדְמָתוֹ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וַֽעֲבָדָ֖הּ וְיָ֥שַׁב בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the nation which will bring its neck into [the] yoke of [the] king of Babylon and serve him, and I will leave it on its land, declaration of Yahweh, and it will work it and dwell in it.

en.L: But the nation that brings its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him, I will let it remain on its own land, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and it will work it and live in it.'"
en.B: But any nation that bows its neck to the king of Babylon's yoke and serves him, I will leave on its own land, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They will farm it and live there.'"
en.R: But if a nation accepts the rule of the king of Babylon and serves him, I will let it stay in its own land, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Its people will farm the land and live there.'"

es.L: Pero a la nación que meta su cuello bajo el yugo del rey de Babilonia y le sirva, la dejaré en su propia tierra, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y la cultivará y habitará en ella”».
es.B: Pero a toda nación que doble su cuello bajo el yugo del rey de Babilonia y le sirva, la dejaré en su propia tierra, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. La cultivarán y vivirán en ella”».
es.R: Pero si una nación acepta el gobierno del rey de Babilonia y le sirve, la dejaré quedarse en su propia tierra, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Su gente cultivará la tierra y vivirá allí”».

sw.L: Lakini taifa litakalotia shingo yake chini ya nira ya mfalme wa Babeli na kumtumikia, nitaliacha katika nchi yake, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nalo litailima na kukaa ndani yake.'"
sw.B: Lakini taifa lolote litakaloinamisha shingo yake chini ya nira ya mfalme wa Babeli na kumtumikia, nitaliacha katika nchi yake, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Watu wake wataliima na kuishi humo.'"
sw.R: Lakini taifa likikubali utawala wa mfalme wa Babeli na kumtumikia, nitaliacha libaki katika nchi yake, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Watu wake watalima nchi hiyo na kuishi humo.'"

decisions.choice: work it: farm the land
decisions.reason: The verb is the same as "serve". Used of the ground it means to till it (Genesis 2:5; 4:2). The words play on each other: the nation that serves the king of Babylon will go on working its own land.

decisions.choice: I will leave it on its land: the promise set against the threat of verse 10
decisions.reason: Submission means staying in the land; refusal means being driven out. The message to the kings ends here.

decisions.choice: farm; they, its people (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "farm" for working the land, and "they" for the nation's people.

decisions.choice: single and double quotation marks closed
decisions.reason: The message to the envoys (from verse 4) and God's words to Jeremiah (from verse 2) both end here.

source.text: וְאֶל־צִדְקִיָּ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי כְּכָל־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לֵאמֹ֑ר הָבִ֨יאוּ אֶת־צַוְּארֵיכֶ֜ם בְּעֹ֣ל מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֗ל וְעִבְד֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ וְעַמּ֖וֹ וִֽחְיֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And to Zedekiah king of Judah I spoke according to all the words the these, saying: bring your necks into [the] yoke of [the] king of Babylon and serve him and his people and live.

en.L: And to Zedekiah king of Judah I spoke according to all these words, saying, "Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live.
en.B: I said the same things to Zedekiah king of Judah: "Bow your necks to the king of Babylon's yoke. Serve him and his people, and you will live.
en.R: I gave the same message to Zedekiah king of Judah. I said, "Put your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon and accept his rule. Serve him and his people, and you will stay alive.

es.L: Y a Sedequías, rey de Judá, hablé conforme a todas estas palabras, diciendo: «{{plural_you:Metan sus cuellos|Meted vuestros cuellos}} bajo el yugo del rey de Babilonia, y {{plural_you:sírvanle|servidle}} a él y a su pueblo, y {{plural_you:vivan|vivid}}.
es.B: Le dije lo mismo a Sedequías, rey de Judá: «{{plural_you:Doblen sus cuellos|Doblad vuestros cuellos}} bajo el yugo del rey de Babilonia. {{plural_you:Sírvanle|Servidle}} a él y a su pueblo, y {{plural_you:vivirán|viviréis}}.
es.R: Le di el mismo mensaje a Sedequías, rey de Judá. Le dije: «{{plural_you:Pongan sus cuellos|Poned vuestros cuellos}} bajo el yugo del rey de Babilonia y {{plural_you:acepten|aceptad}} su gobierno. {{plural_you:Sírvanle|Servidle}} a él y a su pueblo, y {{plural_you:seguirán|seguiréis}} con vida.

sw.L: Na kwa Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda nilisema sawasawa na maneno haya yote, nikisema, "Tieni shingo zenu chini ya nira ya mfalme wa Babeli, mkamtumikie yeye na watu wake, mkaishi.
sw.B: Nilimwambia Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda mambo hayo hayo: "Inamisheni shingo zenu chini ya nira ya mfalme wa Babeli. Mtumikieni yeye na watu wake, nanyi mtaishi.
sw.R: Nilimpa Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda ujumbe uleule. Nilisema, "Tieni shingo zenu chini ya nira ya mfalme wa Babeli, mkubali utawala wake. Mtumikieni yeye na watu wake, nanyi mtabaki hai.

decisions.choice: according to all these words: the same message given to the foreign kings
decisions.reason: Jeremiah repeats to his own king what he sent to the neighboring kings in verses 4-11. Zedekiah is the king the envoys had come to (verse 3).

decisions.choice: your necks ... and live: the king and his people addressed together; the last command gives the result
decisions.reason: The commands are plural, for Zedekiah and his people (verse 13). After "bring" and "serve", "and live" is the promised outcome of obeying, as in Amos 5:4.

decisions.choice: bring your necks under the yoke: submit to the king of Babylon's rule
decisions.reason: As in verse 8, the picture is the yoke Jeremiah wears.

decisions.choice: you will live (Balanced); you will stay alive (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the result that the last command implies (see m2). Readable adds "accept his rule" to explain the yoke. Jeremiah's words to Zedekiah open a double quotation mark that stays open to the end of verse 15.

decisions.choice: plural you to Zedekiah
decisions.reason: The king and his people are addressed together (meaning decision m2), so the commands are plural and take plural_you spans.

source.text: לָ֤מָּה תָמ֨וּתוּ֙ אַתָּ֣ה וְעַמֶּ֔ךָ בַּחֶ֖רֶב בָּרָעָ֣ב וּבַדָּ֑בֶר֙ כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־הַגּ֕וֹי אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יַעֲבֹ֖ד אֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Why will you die, you and your people, by the sword, by the famine and by the pestilence, as has spoken Yahweh concerning the nation which not will serve [the] king of Babylon?

en.L: Why will you die, you and your people, by the sword, by famine and by pestilence, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken concerning the nation that will not serve the king of Babylon?
en.B: Why should you and your people die by sword, famine and plague, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said will happen to any nation that will not serve the king of Babylon?
en.R: Why should you and your people die by war, famine and disease? That is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said will happen to any nation that refuses to serve the king of Babylon.

es.L: ¿Por qué {{plural_you:morirán|moriréis}}, tú y tu pueblo, por la espada, por el hambre y por la peste, como ha dicho {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} acerca de la nación que no sirva al rey de Babilonia?
es.B: ¿Por qué {{plural_you:han|habéis}} de morir tú y tu pueblo por la espada, el hambre y la peste, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dicho que le pasará a toda nación que no sirva al rey de Babilonia?
es.R: ¿Por qué {{plural_you:han|habéis}} de morir tú y tu pueblo en la guerra, de hambre y de enfermedades? Eso es lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dicho que le pasará a cualquier nación que se niegue a servir al rey de Babilonia.

sw.L: Kwa nini mfe, wewe na watu wako, kwa upanga, kwa njaa na kwa tauni, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyonena juu ya taifa lisilotaka kumtumikia mfalme wa Babeli?
sw.B: Kwa nini wewe na watu wako mfe kwa upanga, njaa na tauni, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyosema litakavyolipata taifa lolote lisilotaka kumtumikia mfalme wa Babeli?
sw.R: Kwa nini wewe na watu wako mfe kwa vita, njaa na magonjwa? Hayo ndiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyosema yatalipata taifa lolote linalokataa kumtumikia mfalme wa Babeli.

decisions.choice: why will you die: a plea in the form of a question
decisions.reason: The question urges the king not to choose death when life is offered (verse 12). The verb is plural and "you" is singular: Zedekiah and, with him, his people.

decisions.choice: as the LORD has spoken: the warning of verse 8
decisions.reason: The threat against any nation that will not serve the king of Babylon applies to Judah as much as to its neighbors.

decisions.choice: sword, famine and pestilence (Literal); sword, famine and plague (Balanced); war, famine and disease (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 8. Readable turns the second half of the question into a statement.

source.text: וְאַֽל־תִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶל־דִּבְרֵ֣י הַנְּבִאִ֗ים הָאֹמְרִ֤ים אֲלֵיכֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תַעַבְד֖וּ אֶת־מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֑ל כִּ֣י שֶׁ֔קֶר הֵ֖ם נִבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And do not listen to [the] words of the prophets, the [ones] saying to you, saying: not you will serve [the] king of Babylon, for falsehood they [are] prophesying to you.

en.L: And do not listen to the words of the prophets who are saying to you, 'You shall not serve the king of Babylon,' for they are prophesying a lie to you.
en.B: Do not listen to the words of the prophets who tell you, 'You will not serve the king of Babylon.' They are prophesying a lie to you.
en.R: Do not listen to the prophets who tell you, 'You will not have to serve the king of Babylon.' What they tell you is a lie.

es.L: Y no {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchéis}} las palabras de los profetas que {{plural_you:les|os}} hablan diciendo: “No {{plural_you:servirán|serviréis}} al rey de Babilonia”, porque {{plural_you:les|os}} profetizan mentira.
es.B: No {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchéis}} las palabras de los profetas que {{plural_you:les|os}} dicen: “No {{plural_you:servirán|serviréis}} al rey de Babilonia”. Lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} profetizan es mentira.
es.R: No {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchéis}} a los profetas que {{plural_you:les|os}} dicen: “No {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} que servir al rey de Babilonia”. Lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} dicen es mentira.

sw.L: Wala msiyasikilize maneno ya manabii wanaowaambia, wakisema, 'Hamtamtumikia mfalme wa Babeli,' kwa maana wanawatabiria uongo.
sw.B: Msiyasikilize maneno ya manabii wanaowaambia, 'Hamtamtumikia mfalme wa Babeli.' Wanawatabiria uongo.
sw.R: Msiwasikilize manabii wanaowaambia, 'Hamtalazimika kumtumikia mfalme wa Babeli.' Wanayowaambia ni uongo.

decisions.choice: the prophets: Judah's own prophets, who say what the foreign advisers say
decisions.reason: The message matches verses 9-10, now turned on the prophets of Judah. Chapter 28 tells of one of them, Hananiah, who promised that the yoke of Babylon would be broken within two years (28:2-4).

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for the prophets' words
decisions.reason: They stand inside Jeremiah's quoted words to Zedekiah. Readable says "will not have to serve", as in verse 9.

source.text: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א שְׁלַחְתִּים֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְהֵ֛ם נִבְּאִ֥ים בִּשְׁמִ֖י לַשָּׁ֑קֶר לְמַ֨עַן הַדִּיחִ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ וַאֲבַדְתֶּ֔ם אַתֶּ֕ם וְהַנְּבִאִ֖ים הַֽנִּבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For not I sent them, declaration of Yahweh, and they [are] prophesying in my name falsely, so as I drive out you and you perish, you and the prophets, the [ones] prophesying to you.

en.L: For I have not sent them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they are prophesying falsely in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, so that I will drive you out and you will perish, you and the prophets who are prophesying to you."
en.B: I did not send them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They are prophesying lies in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and the result will be that I drive you out and you perish, you and the prophets who prophesy to you."
en.R: I did not send them, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They are using {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name to tell lies. Their lies will lead to this: I will drive you out, and you will die, both you and the prophets who speak to you."

es.L: Porque yo no los envié, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y ellos profetizan falsamente en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, para que yo {{plural_you:los|os}} eche y {{plural_you:perezcan|perezcáis}}, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y los profetas que {{plural_you:les|os}} profetizan».
es.B: Yo no los envié, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Ellos profetizan mentiras en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, y el resultado será que yo {{plural_you:los|os}} eche y {{plural_you:perezcan|perezcáis}}, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y los profetas que {{plural_you:les|os}} profetizan».
es.R: Yo no los envié, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Están usando {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre para decir mentiras. Sus mentiras llevarán a esto: yo {{plural_you:los|os}} echaré y {{plural_you:morirán|moriréis}}, tanto {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} como los profetas que {{plural_you:les|os}} hablan».

sw.L: Kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} sikuwatuma, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nao wanatabiri uongo kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, ili niwafukuze nanyi mwangamie, ninyi na manabii wanaowatabiria."
sw.B: Sikuwatuma, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wanatabiri uongo kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, na matokeo yake ni kwamba nitawafukuza nanyi mtaangamia, ninyi na manabii wanaowatabiria."
sw.R: Sikuwatuma, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wanalitumia jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} kusema uongo. Uongo wao utaleta jambo hili: nitawafukuza, nanyi mtakufa, ninyi pamoja na manabii wanaowaambia hayo."

decisions.choice: I have not sent them, declares the LORD: Jeremiah gives God's own words
decisions.reason: There is no new "Thus says the LORD"; "declares the LORD" marks these as God's words within Jeremiah's speech to the king.

decisions.choice: prophesying in my name falsely: claiming God's authority for a lie
decisions.reason: To speak in God's name is to speak as his messenger. The charge against these prophets is the one made in 14:14-15 and 23:21, 25: God did not send them, yet they claim to speak for him.

decisions.choice: so that I will drive you out: the result of listening to them
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, the word gives the outcome, not the prophets' intention. The prophets share the fate of those who believe them (14:15-16).

decisions.choice: the result will be (Balanced); their lies will lead to this (Readable)
decisions.reason: These wordings give the sense of result (see m3). The quotation opened at verse 12 closes here.

source.text: וְאֶל־הַכֹּהֲנִים֩ וְאֶל־כָּל־הָעָ֨ם הַזֶּ֜ה דִּבַּ֣רְתִּי לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ אַֽל־תִּשְׁמְע֞וּ אֶל־דִּבְרֵ֣י נְבִֽיאֵיכֶ֗ם הַֽנִּבְּאִ֤ים לָכֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֨ה כְלֵ֧י בֵית־יְהוָ֛ה מוּשָׁבִ֥ים מִבָּבֶ֖לָה עַתָּ֣ה מְהֵרָ֑ה כִּ֣י שֶׁ֔קֶר הֵ֖מָּה נִבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And to the priests and to all the people the this I spoke, saying: thus says Yahweh: do not listen to [the] words of your prophets, the [ones] prophesying to you, saying: look, [the] vessels of [the] house of Yahweh [are] being brought back from Babylon now quickly, for falsehood they [are] prophesying to you.

en.L: And to the priests and to all this people I spoke, saying, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Do not listen to the words of your prophets who are prophesying to you, saying, 'Look, the vessels of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will now shortly be brought back from Babylon,' for they are prophesying a lie to you.
en.B: Then I spoke to the priests and to all this people: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Do not listen to what your prophets are prophesying to you: 'The vessels of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will very soon be brought back from Babylon.' They are prophesying a lie to you.
en.R: Then I spoke to the priests and to all the people. I said, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Do not listen to your prophets who tell you, 'Very soon the things that were taken from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple will be brought back from Babylon.' What they tell you is a lie.

es.L: Y a los sacerdotes y a todo este pueblo hablé, diciendo: «Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: No {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchéis}} las palabras de {{plural_you:sus profetas|vuestros profetas}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} profetizan, diciendo: “He aquí, los utensilios de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} serán devueltos de Babilonia ahora, muy pronto”, porque {{plural_you:les|os}} profetizan mentira.
es.B: Luego hablé a los sacerdotes y a todo este pueblo: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: No {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchéis}} lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} profetizan {{plural_you:sus profetas|vuestros profetas}}: “Los utensilios de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} serán devueltos de Babilonia muy pronto”. Lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} profetizan es mentira.
es.R: Luego hablé a los sacerdotes y a todo el pueblo. Les dije: «Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: No {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchéis}} a {{plural_you:sus profetas|vuestros profetas}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} dicen: “Muy pronto traerán de vuelta de Babilonia las cosas que se llevaron del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}”. Lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} dicen es mentira.

sw.L: Na kwa makuhani na kwa watu hawa wote nilisema, nikisema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Msiyasikilize maneno ya manabii wenu wanaowatabiria, wakisema, 'Tazama, vyombo vya nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} vitarudishwa kutoka Babeli sasa upesi,' kwa maana wanawatabiria uongo.
sw.B: Kisha niliwaambia makuhani na watu hawa wote: "Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Msisikilize yale manabii wenu wanayowatabiria: 'Vyombo vya nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} vitarudishwa kutoka Babeli karibuni sana.' Wanawatabiria uongo.
sw.R: Kisha nilizungumza na makuhani na watu wote. Nilisema, "Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Msiwasikilize manabii wenu wanaowaambia, 'Karibuni sana vitu vilivyochukuliwa kutoka hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} vitarudishwa kutoka Babeli.' Wanayowaambia ni uongo.

decisions.choice: the vessels of the house of the LORD: the temple treasures taken to Babylon in 597 BC
decisions.reason: When Nebuchadnezzar took King Jehoiachin (Jeconiah) into exile, he carried off the treasures of the temple and the palace (2 Kings 24:13). The prophets promised that these would soon come home, as Hananiah did, giving two years (28:3).

decisions.choice: verses 16-22 in their longer Hebrew form
decisions.reason: The Greek translation gives verses 16-22 in a much shorter form. It has no verse 17, it names the things left in Jerusalem more briefly and does not list them in the same way (verses 19-21), and it ends with the vessels going to Babylon, without the promise in verse 22 that God will bring them back. Jeremiah in Greek is shorter in many places (see 1:1). The Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: now shortly: within a short time
decisions.reason: The two words together stress how soon the return is promised. In 28:3 Hananiah sets it within two years.

decisions.choice: vessels (Literal, Balanced); the things that were taken (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word covers every kind of article or utensil. Readable says what these were: the things taken from the temple, as 2 Kings 24:13 tells. Jeremiah's words open a double quotation mark that stays open to the end of verse 22, and the prophets' words inside take single marks.

decisions.choice: los utensilios
decisions.reason: The temple vessels (meaning decision m1) are "utensilios" at Literal and Balanced, as published for the temple furnishings in Kings and Chronicles; Readable says "las cosas que se llevaron del templo".

source.text: אַל־תִּשְׁמְע֣וּ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם עִבְד֥וּ אֶת־מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל וִֽחְי֑וּ לָ֧מָּה תִֽהְיֶ֛ה הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את חָרְבָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not listen to them; serve [the] king of Babylon and live. Why will become the city this a ruin?

en.L: Do not listen to them; serve the king of Babylon, and live. Why should this city become a ruin?
en.B: Do not listen to them. Serve the king of Babylon and you will live. Why should this city be turned into a ruin?
en.R: Do not listen to them. Serve the king of Babylon, and you will stay alive. Why should this city be left in ruins?

es.L: No los {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchéis}}; {{plural_you:sirvan|servid}} al rey de Babilonia, y {{plural_you:vivan|vivid}}. ¿Por qué ha de convertirse esta ciudad en ruinas?
es.B: No los {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchéis}}. {{plural_you:Sirvan|Servid}} al rey de Babilonia y {{plural_you:vivirán|viviréis}}. ¿Por qué ha de quedar esta ciudad convertida en ruinas?
es.R: No los {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchéis}}. {{plural_you:Sirvan|Servid}} al rey de Babilonia, y {{plural_you:seguirán|seguiréis}} con vida. ¿Por qué ha de quedar esta ciudad en ruinas?

sw.L: Msiwasikilize; mtumikieni mfalme wa Babeli, mkaishi. Kwa nini mji huu uwe magofu?
sw.B: Msiwasikilize. Mtumikieni mfalme wa Babeli nanyi mtaishi. Kwa nini mji huu ugeuzwe kuwa magofu?
sw.R: Msiwasikilize. Mtumikieni mfalme wa Babeli, nanyi mtabaki hai. Kwa nini mji huu uachwe ukiwa magofu?

decisions.choice: serve ... and live: the promise given to the king, now to the people
decisions.reason: As in verse 12, the last command gives the result of obeying the first.

decisions.choice: why should this city become a ruin: a plea, as in verse 13
decisions.reason: The question shows what is at stake: not the vessels already taken, but the city itself.

decisions.choice: verse 17 is part of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Greek translation has no verse 17 (see verse 16). The Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: you will live (Balanced); you will stay alive (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 12.

source.text: וְאִם־נְבִאִ֣ים הֵ֔ם וְאִם־יֵ֥שׁ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אִתָּ֑ם יִפְגְּעוּ־נָא֙ בַּֽיהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת לְבִלְתִּי־בֹ֜אוּ הַכֵּלִ֣ים׀הַנּוֹתָרִ֣ים בְּבֵית־יְהוָ֗ה וּבֵ֨ית מֶ֧לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֛ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And if prophets they [are], and if there is [the] word of Yahweh with them, let them entreat please Yahweh of hosts not to go the vessels, the [ones] remaining in [the] house of Yahweh and [the] house of [the] king of Judah and in Jerusalem, to Babylon.

en.L: And if they are prophets, and if the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with them, let them plead now with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts that the vessels that are left in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and [in] the house of the king of Judah and in Jerusalem may not go to Babylon.
en.B: If they really are prophets and have the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with them, they should plead with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies that the vessels still left in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in the palace of Judah's king and in Jerusalem may not go to Babylon.
en.R: If they really are prophets and have a message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, they should pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. They should ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} not to let the things still left in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple, in the king's palace and in Jerusalem be taken to Babylon.

es.L: Y si son profetas, y si la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} está con ellos, que supliquen ahora {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} de los ejércitos que los utensilios que quedan en la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y [en] la casa del rey de Judá, y en Jerusalén, no vayan a Babilonia.
es.B: Si de verdad son profetas y tienen la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, que supliquen {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos que los utensilios que todavía quedan en la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, en el palacio del rey de Judá y en Jerusalén no sean llevados a Babilonia.
es.R: Si de verdad son profetas y tienen un mensaje {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, que oren {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos. Que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pidan que no deje que se lleven a Babilonia las cosas que todavía quedan en el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, en el palacio del rey y en Jerusalén.

sw.L: Lakini kama wao ni manabii, na kama neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} liko pamoja nao, na wamsihi sasa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi ili vyombo vilivyobaki katika nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na [katika] nyumba ya mfalme wa Yuda na katika Yerusalemu visiende Babeli.
sw.B: Kama kweli wao ni manabii na neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} liko pamoja nao, wamsihi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi ili vyombo vilivyobaki katika nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, katika jumba la mfalme wa Yuda na katika Yerusalemu visipelekwe Babeli.
sw.R: Kama kweli wao ni manabii na wana ujumbe kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wamwombe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi. Wamwombe asiruhusu vitu vilivyobaki katika hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, katika jumba la mfalme na katika Yerusalemu vichukuliwe kwenda Babeli.

decisions.choice: plead with the LORD: pray on the people's behalf, as true prophets did
decisions.reason: The verb means to meet someone with a request, and so to intercede. A prophet brought God's word and also prayed for the people (Genesis 20:7; 1 Samuel 12:23); God told Jeremiah not to pray for them (7:16; 15:1).

decisions.choice: if they are prophets: a challenge, not an admission
decisions.reason: Jeremiah sets a test. Instead of promising the return of what was taken, let them pray that what is left may stay. The words that follow show that it will not.

decisions.choice: the house of the king of Judah: the royal palace

decisions.choice: the pillars, the Sea and the stands: the great bronze works of Solomon's temple
decisions.reason: These are the two pillars at the porch (1 Kings 7:15-22), the great basin called the Sea (1 Kings 7:23-26) and the ten wheeled stands for basins (1 Kings 7:27-37). They were too large to carry off in 597 BC. When Jerusalem fell in 586 BC, the Babylonians broke them up and took the bronze to Babylon (2 Kings 25:13; Jeremiah 52:17).

decisions.choice: a sentence broken off and taken up again
decisions.reason: The sentence begun here is interrupted by the clause of verse 20 and starts again in verse 21, and what the LORD says comes in verse 22.

decisions.choice: the list of items as the Hebrew gives it
decisions.reason: The Greek translation has a shorter wording here (see verse 16). The Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: the sea (Literal), the Sea (Balanced); the bronze pillars, the huge bronze tank called the Sea, the bronze stands on wheels (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:13, Balanced writes "the Sea" as a name, and Readable says what each object was. Literal and Balanced end the verse with a comma because the sentence runs on; Readable ends it here.

decisions.choice: el mar (Literal), el Mar (Balanced); las basas
decisions.reason: The bronze works of Solomon's temple keep the names published in 1 Kings 7 ("el Mar", "las basas"); Readable describes them, as the English does.

decisions.choice: bahari, vitako
decisions.reason: The temple furnishings keep the names of 1 Kings 7 ("bahari", "vitako"); Readable explains them, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Jeconiah: King Jehoiachin, taken into exile in 597 BC
decisions.reason: Jeconiah is another form of the name of Jehoiachin, who reigned three months after his father Jehoiakim and was taken to Babylon with his court, the leading men and the craftsmen (2 Kings 24:8-16). Jeremiah also calls him Coniah (22:24).

decisions.choice: nobles: the free-born leading families
decisions.reason: The word names men of rank, the heads of noble families (1 Kings 21:8; Nehemiah 2:16). 2 Kings 24:14-16 tells how these were taken with the king.

decisions.choice: carried ... into exile (Balanced); took ... away as a captive (Readable); the important people (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains what exile meant and says "important people" for the nobles. It makes verse 20 a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: attend to them: take them in hand again for good
decisions.reason: This is the verb translated "punish" in verse 8; here it is used in a good sense, of God turning to care for what he has left for a time. In 29:10 the same verb promises the return of the exiles after seventy years.

decisions.choice: I will bring them up and restore them: fulfilled when Cyrus sent the vessels back
decisions.reason: The vessels did go to Babylon (2 Kings 25:13-17). Ezra 1:7-11 tells how Cyrus king of Persia gave back the temple vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken. "Bring up" is the usual word for the journey up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the promise of return is part of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Greek translation ends with the vessels going to Babylon and has no promise that they will be brought back (see verse 16). The Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: the day I come for them (Balanced); the time I act to bring them home (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the good sense of the verb (see m1). The quotation opened at verse 16 closes here.
